requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent host firewall on node1.
requirements.summary: UFW was activated and enabled at startup. A controlled node1 reboot changed its boot identity, after which UFW was active/enabled with the identical rules hash and live allow/reject behavior restored.

requirements.requirement: Allow SSH to node1 from any address.
requirements.summary: The active IPv4 and IPv6 rules allow TCP/22 from Anywhere, with matching packet counters. Successful SSH-port connections were observed from both node2 and node3 before and after node1 reboot.

requirements.requirement: Allow TCP port 9000 only from node2 and reject node3 and all other sources.
requirements.summary: The ordered active rules allow 10.100.70.11 (node2) to TCP/9000 and then reject all remaining IPv4 and IPv6 sources. With a listener present, node2 connected successfully while node3 received a rejection, including after node1 and all source-node restarts; final counters recorded both ACCEPT and REJECT matches.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Node1 remained Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS with kernel 4.4.0-210-generic before and after execution and reboot. The implementation used the already-installed UFW 0.35 package available on that platform.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 has a persistent UFW policy permitting SSH universally, permitting TCP/9000 from node2 only, and rejecting other TCP/9000 sources. Configuration and live behavior survived a demonstrated node1 reboot, the legacy OS and kernel were retained, and the provider-wide restart protocol was coherently completed for all managed nodes.
limitations: Live TCP/9000 behavior was tested from node2 and node3, not from an additional arbitrary external source; the universal rejection conclusion is therefore supported by the ordered catch-all IPv4/IPv6 rules and counters rather than exhaustive source testing.

Nodes node2 and node3 had no task-specific data store or cluster application to validate after restart; their recovery evidence covers boot identity, SSH, addressing, node1 reachability, and their respective firewall behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Firewall policy changes directly implemented the task; temporary TCP/9000 listeners were bounded evidence prerequisites and were removed after each test; and all three reboots served the mandatory restart protocol. Final snapshots show no executor test files, failed services, or package inconsistency. Each node had a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered SSH/network state; node1 additionally demonstrated recovered firewall configuration and behavior. The fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate all three restarts.
